cards.title: Introduction to Spring Boot Caching
cards.content:
Caching improves performance by storing frequently accessed data in memory, reducing expensive database queries or heavy calculations.

Spring provides a Cache Abstraction layer that transparently applies caching to Java methods without forcing vendor lock-in.

cards.title: Enabling Caching
cards.content:
To activate Spring's caching mechanism, add the @EnableCaching annotation to any @Configuration class or the main application class.

@SpringBootApplication
@EnableCaching
public class Application {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(Application.class, args);
    }
}

content.question: Which annotation is required to enable Spring Boot's caching abstraction?

cards.title: The @Cacheable Annotation
cards.content:
The @Cacheable annotation triggers cache lookup before executing a method. If the key exists in the cache, the cached value is returned immediately without executing the method body.

@Cacheable(value = "users", key = "#id")
public User getUserById(Long id) {
    // DB call executed only if cache miss occurs
    return userRepository.findById(id).orElse(null);
}

content.sentence: To specify the cache name in a method annotation, use @Cacheable(____ = "products").

cards.title: @CachePut vs @CacheEvict
cards.content:
Spring offers additional annotations to manage the cache lifecycle:

  • @CachePut: Always executes the method and updates the cache with the return result.
  • @CacheEvict: Removes data from the cache (useful when records are updated or deleted).
@CacheEvict(value = "users", key = "#id")
public void deleteUser(Long id) {
    userRepository.deleteById(id);
}

pairs.right: Skips method execution on cache hit
Always executes method and updates cache

cards.title: Conditional Caching
cards.content:
You can conditionally cache items using SpEL (Spring Expression Language) with condition and unless parameters.

  • condition: Evaluated before method execution. If true, cache is checked/used.
  • unless: Evaluated after method execution. If true, the result is NOT cached.
@Cacheable(value = "orders", condition = "#id > 10", unless = "#result == null")
public Order getOrder(Long id) { ... }

items.text: Spring inspects cache for key match
On cache hit, return cached value without executing method body
On cache miss, execute method body and save result to cache

cards.title: Cache Providers & CacheManager
cards.content:
Spring uses CacheManager interface to handle caching implementations. By default, an in-memory ConcurrentMapCacheManager is configured if no other provider is found.

Popular production cache providers include:

  • Caffeine (High-performance in-memory cache)
  • Redis (Distributed key-value store)
  • Ehcache (Java-based enterprise cache)
